head: working-tree
subject: HTTP/1 request-head parsing fast paths
change: Method.parse dispatches on the method length and first byte before comparing registered method names, so a parsed start line no longer tests up to ten full slices. A shared LineIterator replaces std.mem.splitSequence for HTTP/1 head and trailer lines: it scans for the first CR with the SIMD single-byte search and checks the next byte for LF, preserving exact split-on-CRLF semantics without the generic two-byte substring search. The head terminator search scans for the first CR and checks the following bytes for CRLFCRLF instead of using the generic four-byte substring search; the request, response and owned-head entry points share the helper. All changes preserve the accepted grammar and first-match semantics. The strict request-line parser now locates its two SP delimiters with the SIMD scalar search and rejects empty fields or extra separators directly, keeping the generic multi-space loop only for the opt-in compatibility mode.

rejected_scalar_line_iterator.note: A byte-at-a-time CR scan was slower than the SIMD single-byte search and was reverted.

http_external_clients.note: curl/nghttp2 HTTP/1.1 and h2 clients against netz after the parser change

notes: One earlier eight-pair head-end batch ran while unrelated ReleaseSafe builds saturated the host and reported inflated absolute times; it was discarded. The reported pairs were repeated on a quieter host with alternating fixed binaries. The owned scenarios include header and body cloning, so the parse-only gain is diluted there. Replacing the CRLF split iterator removed the generic two-byte substring search: the profile's mem.eql share fell from 31% to 1.7% and findPos disappeared, while the SIMD single-byte CR scan became the remaining line-scan cost. A byte-at-a-time CR scan was measured and rejected at 0.938-0.953x. The method dispatch preserves the case-sensitive registered-method set and still routes unknown tokens through the existing extension validation. The head-end helper and LineIterator return the same first match as the standard split/search implementations; the HTTP/1 suite, parser fuzz replay and external curl/nghttp2 interop pass. The strict request-line fast path is neutral on the short origin-form target and improves the longer absolute-form target by 1.2-2.8%, because the delimiter search no longer walks the target byte by byte.
